note: One row per payment system. Each field is a role, not a route. 'Not covered here' means the atlas has not verified it.

systems.name: Lynx
systems.final: Bank of Canada accounts, in real time
systems.finality: Each payment settles individually and is final when posted to participants' Bank of Canada settlement accounts.
systems.direct: Direct participants that hold a Bank of Canada settlement account.
depends: Swift for payment messages, per Payments Canada

systems.name: ACSS
systems.final: Bank of Canada accounts, net, later
systems.finality: Obligations are netted. Net interbank positions settle using Bank of Canada accounts.
systems.direct: Direct clearers. Indirect participants rely on a direct clearer.

systems.name: Real-Time Rail
systems.account: Bank of Canada, under its RTR settlement-account policy
systems.finality: Not live. Payments Canada targets a phased launch from Q4 2026, with Interac e-Transfer clearing and settlement migrating in 2027.
systems.direct: Initial direct participants first, per the launch plan.
systems.nonbank: The Bank of Canada has an eligibility policy for RTR settlement accounts. Eligibility is not proof of a live account.

systems.name: Interac e-Transfer
systems.owner: Interac Corp., owned by banks, credit unions, caisses and acquirers
systems.account: Interac does not hold customer funds. The sending institution holds them until deposit.
systems.finality: The Interac message and funds availability are separate from interbank settlement. That settlement is planned to move to RTR from 2027.
systems.direct: Direct connectors, indirect connectors and downstream entities have different roles.
depends: Real-Time Rail for interbank clearing and settlement, planned from 2027

systems.name: Fedwire Funds
systems.final: Reserve Bank master accounts, in real time
systems.finality: Each payment is final when credited to the receiving institution's master account.
systems.direct: Institutions with a Reserve Bank master account.

systems.name: FedNow
systems.final: Reserve Bank master accounts, in real time
systems.finality: Each payment settles through the Federal Reserve service in master accounts. It is a separate service from Fedwire.
systems.direct: Eligible institutions send and receive. Other institutions can act as liquidity providers or settlement agents.
systems.nonbank: Certified technology providers can connect participants. Certification does not give them a settlement account.

systems.name: ACH
systems.owner: Two operators: FedACH (Federal Reserve) and EPN (The Clearing House)
systems.finality: Batches are netted and settled in master accounts on set schedules.

systems.name: RTP
systems.final: RTP ledger, backed at a Federal Reserve Bank
systems.owner: The Clearing House, owned by large commercial banks
systems.account: A prefunded balance account at a Federal Reserve Bank, held for funding participants. TCH's settlement note names the New York Fed.
systems.finality: Final when the RTP system records the debit and credit to participants' positions. TCH acts as agent on the account and does not hold the balances.
systems.direct: Eligible depository institutions, including credit unions. TCH ownership is not required.
depends: Fedwire, or the Fed's liquidity management transfer service, to fund the prefunded account
A prefunded account at a Federal Reserve Bank

systems.name: CHIPS
systems.final: CHIPS records, backed at the New York Fed
systems.owner: The Clearing House, owned by large commercial banks
systems.account: The CHIPS prefunded balance account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, held for funding participants.
systems.finality: Final when CHIPS releases and settles the payment on its own records. TCH acts as agent on the account and does not own the balances.
systems.direct: CHIPS participants, which are banking institutions with funding obligations.
depends: Fedwire to fund the prefunded account
The prefunded account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York

systems.name: Pix
systems.final: Banco Central do Brasil accounts, in real time
systems.operator: Banco Central do Brasil, which runs SPI for settlement and DICT for keys
systems.account: Direct participants hold dedicated accounts at Banco Central do Brasil, used by SPI.
systems.finality: Payments between different direct participants settle in SPI on the central bank's books. Payments between customers of the same participant can settle on its own systems.
systems.direct: Direct participants hold a settlement account in SPI. Indirect participants settle through one.
systems.nonbank: Eligible payment institutions can take part. Offering Pix is not proof of direct SPI access.
depends: SPI for settlement and DICT for keys, both run by the central bank

systems.name: UPI
systems.owner: NPCI, a not-for-profit owned by banks and other payment institutions
systems.account: Members' RTGS accounts at the Reserve Bank of India
systems.finality: Customers see the money instantly. NPCI nets obligations between banks and RBI's RTGS posts them as a multilateral net settlement batch.
systems.direct: Banks, as payment service providers and account holders.
systems.nonbank: Third-party apps can run the customer interface. They do not hold the account or settle.
depends: Banks' own accounts for customer balances
